newsitem.title: USA: Key U.S. lawmaker sees China MFN renewal.
newsitem.headline: Key U.S. lawmaker sees China MFN renewal.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey predicted a "decisive" House vote Tuesday in favor of renewal of Most Favored Nation trade status for China.
The House is to vote in the afternoon on a resolution offered by Rep. Gerald Solomon, Republican of New York, which would disapprove President Clinton's decision to extend MFN for China.
"Jerry Solomon's resolution will fail, probably by a decisive vote...I don't think it is going to be down to a handful of votes," Armey, a Texas Republican told reporters.
Armey, who had reconsidered his own support for China MFN, last week announced he would again vote for normal trading relations with the Asian giant.

"It is my own view that if in fact it is the duty of our government to protect people from oppression, we do not do that well by adding our own oppressive restrictions on their exposure to freedom through commerce," Armey said.

He added that Congress will have to take up the issue of China again and would look at other legislation later in the year. "Our concern is about the way the Chinese government oppresses its own people and addresses the issue of religious freedom," he said.

Other lawmakers are considering legislation to address issues of election independence, to require the U.S. government to maintain a list of Chinese political prisoners and publish a list of companies that do business with Chinese military affiliates. It also would deny visas to Chinese officials involved in human rights abuses and engaged in selling high-tech weapons.
